claims.text: The starting coating is a dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy.
The starting coating has coherent phase boundaries between its FCC and BCC regions.
A controlled thermal treatment can alter the density and coherence of FCC/BCC phase boundaries.
Dislocation-mediated creep dominates within the proposed elevated-temperature continuous-loading regime.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces impede dislocation glide under sustained stress.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces impede dislocation climb under sustained stress.
Obstruction by coherent phase boundaries causes dislocation pile-up.
Obstruction by coherent phase boundaries causes stress partitioning.
Dislocation pile-up and stress partitioning reduce the creep deformation rate.
Increasing phase-boundary density and improving FCC/BCC boundary coherence will lower the steady-state creep strain rate relative to a lower-boundary-density baseline.
Increasing phase-boundary density and improving FCC/BCC boundary coherence will reduce cumulative plastic deformation relative to the baseline.
The proposed interface-barrier mechanism requires the phase boundaries to retain their structural integrity during loading.
At very high temperatures or extreme stresses, creep mechanisms other than the proposed dislocation-barrier mechanism may prevail.
The barrier effect of phase boundaries is well supported.
